DartPoints is a privately held colocation operator headquartered at 1601 Elm Street, Suite 3650, Dallas, Texas, founded in the early 2000s. NOVA Infrastructure made a strategic growth investment in the company in 2025.

The company positions itself explicitly around secondary markets, describing its mission as bringing enterprise-grade colocation, cloud, and managed infrastructure to communities outside the largest US metros, with an emphasis on AI-ready, high-density capacity supporting regional economic growth. Its operator site lists 11 facilities across Indiana, Louisiana, North Carolina, Ohio, and South Carolina, naming Columbus, Indiana, Baton Rouge and Shreveport, Louisiana, Asheville, North Carolina, Cincinnati and Dublin, Ohio, and Columbia, Charleston, Greenville, and Spartanburg, South Carolina.

The registry here tracks 10 DartPoints facilities across four states, Indiana, Louisiana, Ohio, and South Carolina, closely matching the operator's own named markets, with North Carolina the one state named on the operator's site not reflected among this registry's current DartPoints rows. As an explicitly Tier 2/Tier 3-focused operator, DartPoints stands apart from the metro-core colocation model of Equinix and CoreSite and the hyperscaler campus model of AWS and Meta recorded elsewhere in this registry, representing smaller-market colocation demand rather than large-scale AI training capacity.
